title: Characterizing Treatment-Context Medication Evidence Across Clinic Notes and Structured EHR Medication History
abstract: arXiv:2608.01570v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Clinic notes may describe medication changes that are not reflected in structured electronic health record (EHR) medication history at the same encounter. Differences in terminology and documentation timing further complicate the interpretation of these discrepancies. We evaluated medication normalization in clinic notes and examined how semantic and temporal matching affected overlap with structured history. A note-grounded reference was constructed from large language model (LLM)-proposed mentions, deterministic canonical projection, and existing targeted correction records; random-audit records were summarized separately. On 5,360 reference mention rows from held-out patients, conditional canonical agreement increased from 81.25% with surface matching to 93.58% after lexical cleanup and curated aliases. translated_title: 刻画临床笔记与结构化电子健康记录用药史中的治疗情境用药证据
translated_abstract: 临床笔记中可能描述了在同一次就诊中未反映在结构化电子健康记录（EHR）用药史中的用药变化。术语差异和记录时间的不同进一步增加了对这些不一致之处的解读难度。我们评估了临床笔记中的用药规范化，并考察了语义匹配和时间匹配如何影响其与结构化用药史的重叠程度。我们基于大语言模型（LLM）提出的用药提及、确定性规范投影以及现有的针对性更正记录，构建了一个以笔记为依据的参考标准；随机审计记录则单独汇总。在来自留出患者的5,360条参考提及记录上，条件规范一致性从表面匹配的81.25%提升至经过词汇清理和人工筛选别名后的93.58%。候选提及与参考提及的对齐进行了单独评估，F1分数为0.6547。在27,552条参考记录上……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该研究构建了以临床笔记为依据的用药参考标准，通过大语言模型提议、确定性规范投影和词汇清理将用药归一化的规范一致性从81.25%提升至93.58%，并量化了语义与时间匹配对临床笔记与结构化EHR用药史重叠程度的影响。
en_tdlr: This study constructed a note-grounded medication reference standard, improving canonical agreement from 81.25% to 93.58% through LLM-proposed mentions, deterministic canonical projection, and lexical curation, while quantifying how semantic and temporal matching affect the overlap between clinic notes and structured EHR medication history.
